notes: Leaf area per unit dry mass. Source units vary widely.

aliases: leaf n;leaf nitrogen;leaf_nitrogen;nitrogen concentration;foliar n;foliar nitrogen
notes: Leaf nitrogen per unit dry mass; check basis carefully.
range_source: Wright et al. 2004 Nature 428:821-827. DOI:10.1038/nature02403; Reich & Oleksyn 2004 PNAS 101:11001-11006. DOI:10.1073/pnas.0403588101; Kattge et al. 2020 TRY. Most plants 10-40 mg/g; N-fixers up to ~60.

aliases: leaf p;leaf phosphorus;leaf_phosphorus;phosphorus concentration;foliar p;foliar phosphorus
notes: Leaf phosphorus per unit dry mass.
range_source: Reich & Oleksyn 2004 PNAS 101:11001-11006. DOI:10.1073/pnas.0403588101; Kattge et al. 2020 TRY. Typical 0.5-5 mg/g; extreme upper ~10.

aliases: leaf c;leaf carbon;leaf_carbon;foliar carbon;foliar c;carbon concentration
notes: Leaf carbon per unit dry mass; often measured alongside N and P.
range_source: Elser et al. 2000 Nature 408:578-580. DOI:10.1038/35046141; Kattge et al. 2020 TRY. Most plant tissue 40-55% C by mass = 400-550 mg/g.

aliases: leaf cn ratio;leaf_cn_ratio;cn ratio;c:n;c n ratio
notes: Leaf carbon to nitrogen ratio; dimensionless; relates to decomposition rate.
range_source: Reich & Oleksyn 2004 PNAS 101:11001-11006. DOI:10.1073/pnas.0403588101. Fast-growing herbs ~5-10; sclerophylls and conifers up to ~200.

notes: Leaf chlorophyll content per unit area; links to remote sensing reflectance.
range_source: Asner et al. 2009 Glob Ecol Biogeogr 18:745-756. DOI:10.1111/j.1466-8238.2009.00474.x. Shade leaves ~60-100; sun leaves ~20-50 ug/cm2.

notes: Mean leaf lifespan in months; links SLA to decomposition rate.
range_source: Reich et al. 1997 PNAS 94:13730-13734. DOI:10.1073/pnas.94.25.13730. Deciduous ~1-8 months; evergreen needles up to ~48 months.

aliases: leaf water content;leaf_water_content;leaf rwc;relative water content;fresh weight dry weight ratio
notes: Leaf water content relative to dry mass; drought tolerance indicator.
range_source: Nolan et al. 2020 Nat Ecol Evol 4:270-279. DOI:10.1038/s41559-019-1060-4. Succulents up to ~30 g/g; sclerophylls ~0.5-2 g/g.

notes: Leaf thickness; may be reported in mm or um.
range_source: Pérez-Harguindeguy et al. 2013 Aust J Bot 61:167-234. DOI:10.1071/BT12225. Most leaves 0.05-1 mm; CAM succulents up to ~20 mm.

notes: Light-saturated net CO2 assimilation rate per unit leaf area.
range_source: Kattge & Knorr 2007 Plant Cell Environ 30:1176-1190. DOI:10.1111/j.1365-3040.2007.01691.x; Kattge et al. 2020 TRY. Shade specialists ~0.5; fast-growing herbs up to ~50-60 umol/m2/s.

notes: Stomatal conductance to water vapor; paired with photosynthesis for WUE.
range_source: Medlyn et al. 2011 Glob Change Biol 17:2134-2144. DOI:10.1111/j.1365-2486.2010.02375.x. Typical operational range 50-500 mmol/m2/s; extremes 0.5-2000.

notes: Wood density; balsa ~0.12; most tropical hardwoods 0.5-0.9; theoretical max ~1.4.
range_source: Chave et al. 2009 Ecol Lett 12:351-366. DOI:10.1111/j.1461-0248.2009.01285.x; Zanne et al. 2009 Dryad Global Wood Density Database. DOI:10.5061/dryad.234.

notes: Some studies separate stem from bulk wood tissue; same physical constraints.

aliases: stem diameter;dbh;diameter breast height;diameter at breast height;trunk diameter;basal diameter;stem dbh
notes: Stem or trunk diameter; dbh most common for trees. Confirm measurement height.
range_source: Chave et al. 2014 Glob Change Biol 20:3177-3190. DOI:10.1111/gcb.12629. Seedlings ~0.01 cm; giant sequoias up to ~1000 cm diameter.

notes: Outer bark thickness; fire resistance and insulation trait.
range_source: Pausas 2015 New Phytol 207:583-585. DOI:10.1111/nph.13349. Thin-barked species ~0.5 mm; fire-adapted thick-barked trees up to ~200 mm.

notes: Number of xylem conduits per mm2 of xylem cross-section; tradeoff with vessel diameter.
range_source: Zanne et al. 2010 Am J Bot 97:519-531. DOI:10.3732/ajb.0900178. Vessel-rich angiosperms up to ~3000; diffuse-porous ~50-500.

aliases: xylem vessel diameter;vessel diameter;conduit diameter;mean vessel diameter;tracheid diameter
notes: Mean xylem conduit lumen diameter; determines conductance by Hagen-Poiseuille (r^4) scaling.
range_source: Wheeler et al. 2005 Am J Bot 92:1588-1600. DOI:10.3732/ajb.92.9.1588. Gymnosperm tracheids ~5-50 um; angiosperm vessels ~10-500 um.

aliases: huber value;huber_value;sapwood area leaf area ratio;sa la ratio
notes: Sapwood cross-sectional area per unit leaf area; hydraulic sufficiency index.
range_source: Tyree & Ewers 1991 New Phytol 119:345-360. DOI:10.1111/j.1469-8137.1991.tb00035.x. Typical range 1e-5 to 1e-2 m2/m2.

notes: Seed mass; often per-seed mean values. Min = orchid dust seeds; max = coco de mer.
range_source: Moles et al. 2005 Science 307:576-580. DOI:10.1126/science.1105809; Kattge et al. 2020 TRY. DOI:10.1111/gcb.14904.

notes: Fruit mass including pericarp; distinct from seed mass. Report basis clearly.
range_source: Moles et al. 2005 Science 307:576-580. DOI:10.1126/science.1105809. Range spans berries ~1 mg to Theobroma/coconut-sized fruits ~5e6 mg.

aliases: plant height;height;max height;plant_height;canopy height;maximum height;plant height (mm);height (mm)
notes: Plant or canopy height; confirm life stage. Min = small mosses; max = tallest Sequoia.
range_source: Díaz et al. 2016 Nature 529:167-171. DOI:10.1038/nature16489; Kattge et al. 2020 TRY; Koch et al. 2004 (tallest Sequoia sempervirens ~116 m).

aliases: specific root length;srl;specific_root_length;root length per mass
notes: Fine root length per unit dry mass; root analog of SLA.
range_source: Weemstra et al. 2016 New Phytol 211:1213-1229. DOI:10.1111/nph.14065. Thin high-SRL roots ~500-1000 m/g; thick storage roots ~1-10 m/g.

aliases: root tissue density;root_tissue_density;rtd;root density;fine root density
notes: Fine root tissue density; root economics spectrum complement to SRL.
range_source: Kramer-Walter et al. 2016 J Ecol 104:796-807. DOI:10.1111/1365-2745.12562. Mycorrhizal fast roots ~0.05-0.2; dense storage roots up to ~1.0 g/cm3.

aliases: p50;xylem p50;hydraulic p50;psi50;p_50;cavitation resistance;water potential at 50 percent loss
notes: Water potential at 50% hydraulic conductivity loss (cavitation vulnerability). Values must be negative MPa.
range_source: Choat et al. 2012 Nature 491:752-755. DOI:10.1038/nature11688. Global range: tropical angiosperms ~-1 MPa; desert shrubs < -10 MPa; most angiosperms -0.5 to -10 MPa.

aliases: p88;xylem p88;psi88;p_88;hydraulic failure threshold;water potential at 88 percent loss
notes: Water potential at 88% hydraulic conductivity loss; practical xylem failure threshold. Values must be negative MPa.
range_source: Domec & Gartner 2001 Tree Physiol 21:1031-1039. DOI:10.1093/treephys/21.14.1031; Choat et al. 2012 Nature 491:752-755. DOI:10.1038/nature11688.

aliases: turgor loss point;tlp;psi_tlp;leaf turgor loss;wilting point;osmotic potential at full turgor
notes: Leaf water potential at cell turgor loss. Values must be negative MPa. Tightly correlated with P50.
range_source: Bartlett et al. 2012 Ecol Lett 15:393-405. DOI:10.1111/j.1461-0248.2012.01751.x. Most species -0.5 to -4 MPa; extreme xerophytes < -8 MPa.

aliases: stem hydraulic conductivity;ks;stem ks;specific hydraulic conductivity;ksat stem

range_source: Tyree & Ewers 1991 New Phytol 119:345-360. DOI:10.1111/j.1469-8137.1991.tb00035.x. Range across angiosperms and gymnosperms ~0.001-100 kg m-1 s-1 MPa-1.

aliases: leaf specific hydraulic conductivity;kl;leaf ks;leaf area specific conductivity
notes: Hydraulic conductance per unit leaf area; links water supply to photosynthetic demand.
range_source: Meinzer et al. 2009 Tree Physiol 29:429-437. DOI:10.1093/treephys/tpp018. Typical range 1e-5 to 10 kg m-1 s-1 MPa-1.
